category_title: Students focused on mere task completion with ineffective self-regulation
scenario_title: Reading comprehension worksheet with inefficient material management and question skipping
minimal_context: The student is working independently on three preliminary reading comprehension questions about a text titled 'Animals in the Home' during a 4th grade language arts lesson.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please begin answering the three preliminary reading comprehension questions about the text 'Animals in the Home' on your worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pauses for about half a minute before starting to write. She holds the text sheet in her hands under the worksheet and shifts her attention back and forth from one sheet to the other. For the first question, she copies the details exactly but also records superfluous information, including the issue number and both the Hebrew and Gregorian dates of publication.) Only to write the answer.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, keep going with the rest of the worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the instructions for the second question for about half a minute, sits for another minute facing the text sheet without doing anything, and then moves to read the third question.) I went on to do the third question because I saw this was too difficult for me and so that I would not waste time.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Make sure you go back and try to answer the second question: 'What can be learned from these details?' What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Returns to the second question. She looks at the assignment sheet while holding her head between her hands, reads the text, returns to the assignment sheet, wipes her nose, picks up her pencil, and puts it down. She sits for a relatively long time without asking for help.) I tried to find out the answer… I didn’t understand the question.

task.content: Answering three preliminary reading comprehension questions about a text titled 'Animals in the Home' on a worksheet, including the second question: 'What can be learned from these details?'

context.environment: Regular classroom setting during a 4th grade language arts lesson

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Attempting to answer a difficult question on a reading comprehension worksheet after previously skipping it
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Looked at the assignment sheet while holding her head between her hands, read the text, returned to the assignment sheet, wiped her nose, picked up her pencil, put it down. Took a relatively long time... she did not ask for help.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Felt she did not understand the question, which indicates monitoring of understanding. However, this monitoring and realization of misunderstanding did not lead her to seek help.
related_quotes: I tried to find out the answer… I didn’t understand the question.

behavior_patterns.condition: Beginning a reading comprehension task involving a text sheet and a worksheet
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Paused for about half a minute before starting to write. A few seconds after she began to write, she stopped. She looked at the text sheet under the worksheet... held the text sheet in her hands and shifted her attention back and forth from one sheet to the other instead of placing the two sheets on the table next to each other.

behavior_patterns.condition: Encountering difficulty with the second question of a reading comprehension worksheet
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Looked at the instructions of the second question for about half a minute and then sat for another minute facing the text sheet without doing anything. After a minute and a half of not writing anything, moved to read the third question.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Consciously applied the strategy of skipping problematic questions and went on to the next question.
related_quotes: I went on to do the third question because I saw this was too difficult for me and so that I would not waste time.
I work according to what is easy for me and what is difficult for me I do later on.

behavior_patterns.condition: In response to the first question that asked for locating the main details
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Copied the details exactly. However, she went beyond the information requested and also recorded superfluous information (she included the issue number of the publication as well as both the Hebrew and the Gregorian dates of publication).
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Defined their general goals as obtaining good grades... set goals of task completion and felt successful when they simply filled the space with words.
related_quotes: Whether it was easy or difficult for me …When it is difficult for me to write the answer I know that I’m not succeeding.
